It was really fun experiencing a more arcadey side of this formula. Much of the semi-survival aspects of World are replaced by something more snappy and fast-paced without making major sacrifices to the core game design, and said changes made me experiment surprisingly more than I did with World, namely committing to different weapons, which in my case coming from Insect Glaive, I mained the Hunting Horn, which is a crazy weapon in concept and amazing in execution. The only thing lame about the game are the Rampage mission, which are boring af and needlessly long.

All of this to say that while Rise didn't enamour me the same way MH World did, I had a good time, and I can't wait to start Sunbreak.
I'm sick of fighting Lagombi for the 981247th time for afflicted bones, but other than that it's a pretty good monster hunter.

This is my 2nd MH after MH World.
The wirebugn is really well implemented in this game. This game becomes a fast paced and lots of action packed battle MH (for you and also the monster) with lots of satisfying counter move sets (using certain weapons).

Negative things are of course the NRG on the armor augmentation and talisman that uses gacha mechanic. While rolling nice skills are obviously the goal to always make your build better with so much possibilities but these things also took so long time to get / really laborious to do.
Say you spend 100 hrs in the end game, maybe 20 hrs is just spent for rolling stuffs and then managing your loadouts again. I hope for the endgame in Wilds, they will put the style more in between MHW and MHR.

While very different from the rest of the Monster Hunter franchise you can't deny that Rise has by far the best combat system of all the new gen ones.

Two criticisms for it are the RNG talisman and Qurio crafting, which is just insane... And the fact that while switch skills help weapons be even more unique, it also makes it harder to start learning new weapons once you're used to one, otherwise I love it.

The fights are very fun and have a pretty good level of difficulty, though the base game is pretty lame compared to how amazing the DLC is

I had gotten about 12 hours into Rise the first time when I thought that it wasn't for me. The game was too fast, and I just couldn't react properly to the monsters unlike in World. An issue regarding my skill? Maybe, but I only played GreatSword at the time.
Time passes, time passes. I've finally managed to play through the entire game with my bestie. Got to hr 100 to fight Crimson Glow Valstrax before we decided to move onto Sunbreak. I surprisingly didn't get HR 100 in World or Wilds. This is the first game that has me at HR 100 and over. Rampages were nightmarish alone, but I did not fail. Together? They were amazing, fun, quick ways to jump 4-6 levels up.

This made me a lance player. I love the lance thanks to this game. Looking forward to try Hammer sometime, but also gonna start a second savefile after finishing Sunbreak with dual blades. 

Is this game worth it? 

YES. The answer is YES. Like most MH games. Although it may not click for some players alone, it'll eventually "click" with you through co-op or playing alone. Beautiful game. So peak. This is also the only MH game where I'll casually spend money on the DLCs cosmetics/voices/layered.
Thanks, Capcom!

I got into Monster Hunter when a few friends of mine introduced me to Monster Hunter World. It was awesome. Hunting big monsters with friends, getting to pick my weapon and play style, having a grind which actually felt rewarding when you could make new armor and weaponry using the monster parts you harvested from hunts, and much more. All of that is here in Monster Hunter Rise, as one would expect. It's a decent challenge, too. For someone like me who's still learning to master the concepts, moves, and strategies to most efficiently hunt each creature, this game will test your gamer's skills, patience, and sometimes your sanity. Definitely worth the buy in my book!

I have put over 500 hours into this game between both the PC and Switch versions. I have put an additional 500 hours into Monster Hunter World between PC and PS. I love these games and the Monster Hunter series, and up until very very recently, Capcom was one of my favorite developers. Unfortunately, they have made the absolutely stupid decision to add Enigma DRM to their games, a software which: lowers performance, increases minimum requirements, has historically bricked systems, disables all mods, and is of dubious Russian origin. Until Capcom removes Enigma DRM from this game and all others in their backlog, I cannot in good faith recommend you play it, let alone purchase it. There are already people experiencing issues with the software (some examples including bricking Steam Decks and erasing save data). Until this is fixed, do not play it, do not buy it, and do not let Capcom continue this. If you wish to play this game that badly, either go play it on Switch or "borrow" this game from other sites.

There's really nothing like Monster Hunter and all the attempted genre imitators have failed to capture the magic.

It's the fastest and most action-packed the MonHun formula has been so far with plenty to craft and work towards with engaging fights that never make you feel like you're grinding - it's so much fun running around the map and slapping beasts around that you'll forget in the moment that you're even working toward some crafting goal or quest chain or whatever in the background.

Tons of variety in the weapon movesets that you can truly "play it your way", whether you wanna run in and mash buttons for flashy combos that look cool, be a supportive tank, play with precision hits and dodges, or sit back and enjoy the game as a third-person shooter.

Music and sound are incredible, the graphics of course from a technical standpoint don't live up to the last game due to codevelopment for Switch but the color and art style more than make up for it - you'd have to be the snootiest of fidelity whores to be put off by how this game looks once the fights start moving.

Similar to MHW, but with a handful of changes.

Graphics, while 4K, seem to be less pretty then world (meaning lower powered machines should be able to run MHR)
Maps, Are smaller then MHW. However, you have free movement through the whole map. You can climb almost any wall with the new wall run and wire bug mechanic.
MHR also feel more fast paced when fighting because of the wirebug. The wirebug does make the game feel easier then how it felt in world.

Personally, I think MHR would be a great entry point for a new player to Monster Hunter. And as someone who's put 500 hours into MHW, I find MHR very enjoyable (I also own it in the Switch).

NOTE: if you are coming from MHW, some weapons have been updated/overhauled (looking at you Hunting Horn) and either play slightly different or very different (still looking at you Hunter Horn). If you're not sure about the change, try out the demo!

One of the best action games out there. Slay or capture monsters with 1 of 14 specialized weapons, use monster parts to upgrade said weapons and forge unique armor to build a character that excels at whatever you'd like, then fight a new monster with your new set of gear after gobbling down some delicious-looking dango to give yourself some bonuses for the quest.

Combat has a lot of depth and rewards players for familiarizing themselves with the weapon they use and the monsters they fight. My favorite system in the game was the use of Buddies to customize two cat or dog partners to help with the fighting. You can have a duo of bomb-wielding Palicoes to snatch extra loot from everything it can get its thieving paws on or enlist the aid of crossbow-mounted Palamutes that double as mounts to get you across the map quickly. You can even drift like a Mario Kart game and get that sweet speed boost while riding the dog!
